subject: Proportions for TV units and feature walls
hook: Where should the TV actually go? We work it out from the sofa, not the wall.
ig:
Where should the TV actually go? We work it out from the sofa, not the wall.

This is how we set out a bespoke media wall before a single panel is cut:

Sit where you watch. We measure seated eye height from your own sofa, because that's where the centre of the screen wants to be.

Tape it out. A masking-tape rectangle on the wall shows the screen size and the margin around it. Standing back for ten seconds tells you more than any drawing.

Split the wall. Thirds usually beat halves: a long, low base, then lighter shelving or panelling above.

Check the route. We measure how people walk through the room so the base depth never becomes a shin-catcher.

Only then does it go to the workshop in Hanley to be cut, edged and assembled.

Planning a TV wall this summer? Comment WALL and we'll send you the link to our media wall page.
fb:
Here's a little peek at how we start every media wall: sitting on your sofa with a tape measure.

Seated eye height sets where the screen goes. A tape outline on the wall shows how big it'll feel. Then we split the wall into sensible proportions and check the walkway, all before anything heads to our Hanley workshop to be made.

If you've been staring at a blank chimney breast wondering what to do with it, have a look at our media wall page and get in touch for a free design consultation.
